newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stock mkt index and volume at record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stock mkt index and volume at record.

text.p: Turkish shares surged to the year's 15th record close on Thursday in record volume boosted by the constitutional court's rejection of a challenge to a law enabling the privatisation of Turk Telekom, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 index closed at an all-time high of 1,352, up 101 points, or 8.07 percent above Wednesday's previous high of 1,251.
Daily volume hit a record of 43.46 trillion lira, up from Wednesday's 29.40 trillion and a previous high of 35.89 trillion lira on November 29, 1996.
The court cancelled only a sentence regarding the legal supervision of GSM licence agreements by the Council of State and rejected the rest of the challenge by 116 opposition MPs.

Turkish officials said the decision gave a green light to the sell-off of Telekom or the making of licence agreements for GSMs. The government expects to raise $3.5 billion from Telekom privatisation and another $1 billion from GSM licence agreements later this year.
Brokers said the market's upward movement was expected to continue.
"The rally will continue tomorrow but investors must be aware that some share prices have already risen too much," said Turgay Ozaner from Global securities.
Ozaner said the index would reach "1,500 level soon." The market index has surged 38.5 percent since end-1996.
Of the 237 shares traded today, 211 advanced, only 10 declined and 16 closed stable.
The IMKB Industrial rose 7.01 percent to 1,405, the IMKB Services gained 5.83 percent to 1,306 and the IMKB Financial surged 9.42 percent to 1,336.

Largely state-owned firms were among the top actives-- flat steel maker Eregli, up 2,250 lira at 19,750, Turkish Airlines, up 3,500 lira at 33,500. Utilities Aktas Elektrik rose 17,500 lira to 155,000 lira and Cukurova Elektrik jumped 12,500 lira to at 162,500 lira.
